entities.summary: Maulvi Shahabuddin Delawar is a senior leader of the Taliban and Islamic scholar, born into a prominent Pashtun family in the Kandahar region of Afghanistan. His early education was at the Darul Uloom Haqqania madrasa in Akora Khattak, Pakistan, where he studied Islamic jurisprudence and theology. Delawar's rise to prominence within the Taliban began in the 1990s, as he worked alongside top leaders such as Mullah Omar and Mullah Akhtar Mansour. In 2013, he was appointed as the Taliban's chief propagandist, overseeing the development of the group's propaganda arm and publishing several books on Islamic theology and Taliban ideology. Delawar's leadership within the Taliban has been marked by a series of high-profile attacks, including the 2014 bombing of the Indian embassy in Kabul and the 2019 attack on the Afghan army's headquarters in Kabul. His role in shaping the Taliban's narrative has been significant, and his influence within the group has been felt by many of its top leaders. Despite being one of the most senior Taliban leaders, Delawar remains a relatively opaque figure, with little information available about his personal life or motivations.
